I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My children left for the city — my son works in Handan, my daughter in Shijiazhuang. It's mostly just me now, and my neighbor helps during harvest if I help him back. I have 6 mu of contracted land, including 2 mu from a neighbor who moved away and asked me to work it.

I'm not going to change what I grow. Everyone here does winter wheat then summer maize. The buyers at the grain station know the price, I know the timing, and the land is flat and suited for it. I have access to the irrigation well two fields over through our village agreement. My body is still good enough to manage the spray and the fertilizer bags, though I hire the rotary tiller and combine through the village machinery cooperative — I don't own a tractor.

For wheat, I'll buy 矮抗58 from the township seed station. It's been reliable for me — stiff stems, doesn't lodge, and the local station has been selling it for years. I don't trust new varieties I haven't seen myself. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base before tillage, then top-dress with urea at jointing in March. I irrigate before winter dormancy, again at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain fill if it's dry — that's usually four times. I'll spray herbicide in late February and a fungicide-insecticide mix around heading for powdery mildew and aphids.

For maize, I always buy hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever the station has that's similar and proven. I plant it right after wheat harvest in June, no-till with a small planter I borrow. I fertilize lighter because there's residual from the wheat, and summer rain helps. I irrigate at seedling if it's dry, and again at silking. One herbicide spray early, maybe an insecticide if I see corn borers — but last year I didn't need it.

I expect about 450 kg of wheat per mu and maybe 550 kg of maize. That's normal for here. Not record-breaking, but it pays for what I need.
